title: Mirrors and Convex Lenses
learning_goal: Describe and predict image formation using plane mirrors and thin convex lenses.

stages.title: 1. Plane mirrors
stages.content: A plane mirror forms a virtual image that appears behind the mirror. The image is upright, the same size as the object, and appears the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

stages.title: 2. Convex lenses
stages.content: A convex lens converges parallel light rays toward a focal point. Image properties depend on the object's distance from the lens relative to the focal length.

stages.title: 3. Real and virtual images
stages.content: A real image forms where light rays actually converge and can be projected on a screen. A virtual image forms where rays only appear to originate and cannot be projected on a screen.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: When an object is placed beyond twice the focal length of a convex lens, the image is real, inverted, smaller than the object, and located between one and two focal lengths on the opposite side.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A student stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far behind the mirror does the image appear?
stages.hint: For a plane mirror, image distance equals object distance.
stages.alternate_explanation: The mirror makes the image appear symmetrically located on the other side of the mirror.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, describe plane-mirror images, distinguish real and virtual images, and predict image orientation, size, and location for basic convex-lens positions.

concept_cards.title: Plane mirrors
concept_cards.content: A plane mirror forms a virtual image that appears behind the mirror. The image is upright, the same size as the object, and appears the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

visual.label: Image location follows ray geometry and object position; not every image is real.

concept_cards.title: Convex lenses
concept_cards.content: A convex lens converges parallel light rays toward a focal point. Image properties depend on the object's distance from the lens relative to the focal length.

concept_cards.title: Real and virtual images
concept_cards.content: A real image forms where light rays actually converge and can be projected on a screen. A virtual image forms where rays only appear to originate and cannot be projected on a screen.

concept_cards.title: Where does a plane-mirror image appear relative to the mirror?
concept_cards.content: Reflected rays appear to originate from the virtual image behind the mirror. The image is upright and the same size in the ideal plane-mirror model.

concept_cards.title: Can a virtual image be directly projected onto a screen at its apparent location?
concept_cards.content: Rays only appear to meet at a virtual image. A real image forms where rays actually converge and can be intercepted by a screen.

mastery_check.prompt: A candle is 30 cm in front of an ideal plane mirror. Where is its image?
mastery_check.alternate_explanation: Plane-mirror virtual images appear at equal perpendicular distance behind the reflecting plane.

mastery_check.prompt: A converging lens makes a sharp image on a screen. What type of image is it?
mastery_check.alternate_explanation: Rays actually converge on the screen, which distinguishes a real image.

mastery_check.prompt: A diverging lens views a real object in front of it. In the thin ideal lens model, what image forms?
mastery_check.alternate_explanation: Outgoing rays diverge; backward extensions locate the virtual image on the object side.

mastery_check.prompt: Why do backward ray extensions help locate a virtual image?
choices: They show actual rays traveling backward through space
They show where diverging rays appear to originate
mastery_check.answer: They show where diverging rays appear to originate
accepted_answers: They show where diverging rays appear to originate
mastery_check.alternate_explanation: Extensions are a geometric construction, not additional physical light paths.

mastery_check.prompt: A distant object is imaged by a converging lens. Approximately where does the real image form?
mastery_check.alternate_explanation: Nearly parallel incident rays converge near the focal plane.
